(i) How and when a hypothesis becomes a theory?

‎Hypothesis: An observer organizes observations‏ جس
‎into data form and gives a statement as per experience‏
‎and background knowledge of the event. This statement is‏
‎hypothesis which is tentative explanation of observations‏
‎Repeated exposure of a hypothesis to possible‏
‎falsification increases scientists confidence in the‏
‎hypothesis which is not falsified.‏

‎Theory: Any hypothesis that is tested again and
again without ever being falsified is considered well-
supported. There is soon a series of hypothesis supported
by results of many tests which is then called a theory.

‎(ii) What is hydroponic culture technique? Give its
uses.
۵ Hydroponic culture technique:
Hydroponic culture technique is used to test whether
a certain nutrient is essential for plant or not. In this
technique, the plants are grown in aerated water to which
nutrient mineral salts have been added. Astronauts may
use this technique for growing vegetables.

(xi) How constipation and diarrhoea are caused?
‏جس‎ Diarrehoea: Water and salts are absorbed into the
blood, while undigested material is rejected as faeces. If

to infection, drug action or emotional disturbance, a

‎(ii) Define resolution of eye.

‎E> Resolution of eye:

‎The human naked eye can differentiate between two
points, which are at least 1.0 mm apart. This is known as
resolution. of eye. This resolution can be increased with
the aid of lenses.

‎(iii) | What do you know about multicellular reducers? .
۵ Fungi are eukaryotic multicellular reducers. Fungi
are heterotrophic organisms that are absorptive in their
nutritional mode. Most of them are decomposers that live
on organic material, secrete digestive enzymes and
absorb small organic molecules which are produced by
digestion e.g., Mushrooms.

‎(iv) Define venome.

‎EE Vvenome:

‎The word virus is derived from Latin word venome
meaning, poisonous fluid. It can be defined as non-cellular

‎infectious entities which contain either RNA- and DNA
normally encased in proteinaceous coat reproduce only in
living cells.

‎(v) Define facilitated diffusion and quote one example.
EE some nutrients are carried from the soil to the
epidermal cells of roots through their cell membrane by
facilitated diffusion. In this type of diffusion, carrier
molecules within the cell membrane transport nutrients
across the membrane. These carrier molecules are
proteins, which are present within cell membrane of
epidermal and other root cells.

‎(vi) Explain briefly pox viruses.

‎EX Pox virus: Smallpox is an ancient disease that is
known to have occurred as epidemic in China. and
throughout the whole world. !n smallpox, raised fluid filled
vesicles are formed on the body and become pustules
later on and form pitted scars, the pocks. This disease is
caused by pox virus which is DNA enveloped virus.

‎(vii) | How respiration takes place through cork tissues?
EX In older stems of plant, cork tissue is present which
is formed of dead cells. The cork tissue has special pores
called lenticels which are involved in gaseous exchange
(respiration).

(i) Differentiate between enzyme and coenzyme.
۵ Enzyme: Enzymes are the most important group of
proteins which are biologically active. They increase the
efficiency of a biochemical reaction. Some enzymes
consist solely of proteins. Others also have .non-protein
part.

‎Coenzyme: If the non-protein part of enzyme is

‎loosely attached to the protein part, it is known as

‎coenzyme. It is closely related to vitamins, which
represent the essential raw materials. from which
coenzymes are made.

‎(ii) What is Gram Positive Bacteria?
EX Gram Positive Bacteria:

‎Christain Gram developed the technique of gram
stain. Bacteria could be divided into two groups based on
their response to staining process: ‏نے ۷ای‎

‎1. Gram positive, 2. Gram fegative.

‎By this téchniques, Gram positive bacteria are
stained, purple (retain the primary dye due to formation of
CVI complex). The number of major layers in cell wall of
Gram positive bacteria is 1. Their chemical make up is
peptidoglycan, Teichoic acid and Lipoteichoic acid. Lipids
(1-4%) are present. Overall thickness ranges 20-80 nm,
no outer membrane, and is more permeable than Gram
negative bacteria.

‎(iii) Define Nucleoid.
ES Nucleoid:

‎A bacterial cell unlike the cells of eukaryotic
organisms lacks discrete chromosomes and nuclear
membrane. The nuclear material or DNA in bacterial cell
occupies a position near to the centre of cell. The material
is a single, circular and double standard DNA molecule. It
aggregates as an irregular shaped dense area called the
nucleoid.

‎(iv) | What are causes of asthma?

‎ESD Asthma is a serious respiratory disease associated
with severe peroxysm of difficult breathing, usually
followed by a period of complete relief, with recurrence of
attack at more or less frequent intervals. It is an allergic
reaction to pollen, spores, cold, humidity, pollution, etc.
which manifests itself by spasmodic contraction of sme!!
bronchiole tubes. Asthma results in the release of
inflammatory chemicals such as histamines into the
circulatory system that cause severe contraction of the
bronchiole.

‎0۷) What are functional unit of lungs?

‎Ans 4 During respiration in man, the bronchioles continue
to divide and subdivide deep into the lungs and finally
open into a large number of air-sacs. Air-sac is the
functional unit of the lungs. Each air-sac consists of
several microscopic single-layered structures ء٥٥‎
alveoli. :

‎(vi) Define diffusion.

‎EXD Diffusion:

‎Some nutrients or molecules move along ‏ضر‎
‎concentration gradient through the cell membranes and
cytoplasm. These molecules move from the area of higher
concentration to the area of lower concentration. This
movement of molecules is called diffusion.

‎(vii) What is plasmolysis?
‏تا‎ Plasmolysis:

‎Plasmolysis can be defined as the shrinkage ot
protoplast due to exosmosis of water. When a living cell is
placed in a solution having lower water potential than that
of the cell, plasmolysis takes. place and the cell is called
plasmolysed.

‎(viii) Differentiate between cohesion and adhesion.

‎ES Cohesion: It is the attraction among water
molecules which hold water together, forming a solid
chain-like column within the xylem tubes. The water
molecule form hydrogen bonds between them.

‎Adhesion: It may be added that water molecules
also adhere to the cell wails of xylem cells, so that the
column of water in xylem tissue does not break. The
composition of cell wall provides necessary adhesion to
water molecules that helps water creep up. The cellulose
component of cell wall, especially has great affinity for
water. It can imbibe water.

‎(ix) Define stomatal transpiration.

‎ESD stomatal transpiration: It is a type of transpiration
in which the’ water vapours escape through stomata In
isobilateral leaves, the stomata are present, in both. upper
and lower epidermis e.g., lily and maize leaf

Give the drawbacks to use the period of a
pendulum as a time standard.

۵ (1) The time period of a simple pendulum depends
upon its length and value of ‘g’ at any place. The period of
the pendulum of fixed length may be different at different
places due to the change of ‘g’. As the value of ‘g’
changes at different places, so it will increase or decrease
the time period of the pendulum.

period of the pendulum. As the temperature increases, the
length of the pendulum will increase. Thus the time period
will also increase.

(3) Surrounding atmosphere or are resistance may
affect the time period of simple pendulum.

In the light of above said drawbacks, the time period
of a pendulum cannot be used as time standard.

colours. Explain how does it happen.

‎EX The colours are seen on the oil film spreading over a
wet footpath due to interference of light waves.

‎If white light is incident on an oil film of irregular
thickness at all possible angles, we can see the
interference pattern due to each colour separately. It is
quite possible that at certain place on oil film, its thickness
and angle of incidence are such that the condition of
destructive interference for one of its seven colours is

‎(i)

‎colours show their appearance.

‎As a result, different colours which are seen with —
ordinary light are produced due to interference of waves
reflected from the opposite surfaces of the oil film.

‎(iii) How would you distinguish between un- |
polarized and plane-polarized lights?
EX When un-polarized light is passed through a
polaroid, the emerging light beam has all the electric
vectors: confined in one plane at right angles to its
direction of propagation. Such light is called plane
polarized light (polaroid is named as polarize). When
another polaroid is placed in the path of polarized light
with its axis parallel to the first polaroid, the total light will
pass through the second polaroid. If second polaroid is
rotated through 90°, no light passes through it, but
ordinary or un-polarized light will totally pass through it in
all directions. This second polaroid distinguishes the plane
polarized light from ordinary on un-polarized light. This
polaroid used to test polarized light is called an analyzer.

(iv) One can buy a cheap microscope for use by the
children. The images seen in’ such a
microscope have coloured edges. Why is this
so?

‎- > The images seen in the cheap microscope have

‎coloured edges due to defect of the lenses. Such-a defect
is known as chromatic aberration. A lens acts like two
prisms placed end to end, thisygives rise to dispersion of
light. When rays of white light parallel to. the principle axis
pass through a convex lens, they are dispersed into seven
colotirs\in'such a way that different colours are brought to
focus at different distances from the lens. Since blue rays
are bent more than the red, so focal length for blue is
smaller. Such a lens cannot bring all the rays of white light
from a point on the object to a single point on the image.
As a result, the image is not shaped and is coloured at

‎edges and not clear. This image defect is called chromatic
aberration.

dispersion? Explain.

monochromatic, then the narrow band of wavelengths will
disperse in different directions. When the light signals
enter the glass fibre, the light spreads into different
wavelengths ‏ہ۸‎ A, and ‏ہ۸‎ As 4, meets the core and
cladding at the critical angle and A, and 1, are at slightly
greater angles. The light paths have thus different lengths.
So the light of different wavelengths reaches the other end
of the fibre at different times. In the presence of power
losses due to dispersion and spreading of the light signal,
the information received at the other end of a fibre will be
faulty and distorted.

constant volume. So, we conclude that specific heat at
